questions.q: What quantity does the maximum likelihood estimator maximize?
options: The log-likelihood of the observed data as a function of the parameter θ
The number of parameters in the model
questions.explain: MLE finds the parameter value θ̂ that maximizes ℓ(θ) = log L(θ), the log-likelihood of the data actually observed — the parameter value that makes the observed sample most probable.

questions.q: For X₁,...,Xₙ ~ Exponential(λ) i.i.d., what is the maximum likelihood estimator of λ?
questions.explain: Setting the derivative of ℓ(λ) = n log λ − λΣxᵢ to zero gives λ̂ = n/Σxᵢ = 1/x̄, the reciprocal of the sample mean — consistent with E[X] = 1/λ for the exponential distribution.

questions.q: The MLE for a normal distribution's variance divides the sum of squared deviations by n, while the familiar 'sample variance' formula divides by n−1. What does this tell you?
options: The MLE formula is simply wrong and should never be used
The MLE is slightly biased downward in finite samples; dividing by n−1 corrects that bias
Dividing by n−1 is the maximum likelihood estimator
The two formulas always give identical numerical results
questions.explain: The MLE for variance, Σ(xᵢ−x̄)²/n, has expectation (n−1)/n · σ², a slight downward bias. The n−1 version is the bias-corrected ('unbiased') sample variance, not the raw MLE.

questions.q: A Gamma distribution has mean kθ and variance kθ². Using the Method of Moments with sample mean x̄ = 6 and sample variance s² = 12, what is the MoM estimate of θ?
questions.explain: MoM sets kθ = x̄ and kθ² = s². Dividing gives θ̂ = s²/x̄ = 12/6 = 2.

questions.q: Why is MLE generally preferred over the Method of Moments as a default estimation technique in practice?
options: MLE is always easier to compute by hand
MLE is typically more statistically efficient, using all the information in the likelihood rather than just a few matched moments
The Method of Moments cannot be applied to continuous distributions
questions.explain: Under standard regularity conditions, MLE achieves the lowest possible asymptotic variance among consistent estimators (the Cramér-Rao bound), whereas MoM discards information in the data beyond the matched moments, generally giving higher-variance estimates.
